analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the efficacy of 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy (ALA-PDT) in treating persistent cervical low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) with HPV16/18 infection. A retrospective analysis of 304 patients was conducted, dividing them into three groups: ALA-PDT, LEEP, and observation. The results showed that both ALA-PDT and LEEP had significantly higher LSIL regression and HPV clearance rates compared to the observation group, with no significant difference between ALA-PDT and LEEP. Adverse effects were mild in the ALA-PDT group, while the LEEP group had a 21.43% incidence of cervical stenosis or adhesion. The authors suggest that ALA-PDT is an effective and safe treatment option, especially for young women seeking fertility preservation. The study's limitations include its retrospective design, which may introduce bias, and the moderate evidence strength due to the observational approach.

title: Distribution of high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) genotypes among women with normal cytology and cervical cancer: a hospital-based cross-sectional study in Mysore, India
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major public health burden in India, with persistent infection by high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) recognized as the primary etiological factor. Understanding the distribution of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) genotypes is essential for optimizing screening and vaccination strategies. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence and genotype distribution of HR-HPV among women aged 20–75 years attending tertiary care hospitals in Mysore, Karnataka, India. In this hospital-based cross-sectional study, cervicovaginal lavage (CVL) samples were collected from 172 non-pregnant women aged 20–75 years attending the Obstetrics and Gynecology Departments of JSS Hospital and Cheluvamba Hospital, or the Oncology Department of Krishnarajendra Hospital, Mysore, between August 2021 and March 2023. Cheluvamba hospital and Krishnarajendra hospital belongs to Mysore Medical College and Research Institute (MMCRI), Govt of Karnataka, Karnataka, India. Cytological evaluation was performed using the Papanicolaou (Pap) test. HPV DNA was detected by MY09/MY11 polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and HPV-positive participants were genotyped using the TRUPCR ® HR-HPV Genotyping Kit, which detects 14 high-risk HPV genotypes. Of the 172 participants, 117 (68.0%) had normal cytology, while 55 (32.0%) presented with cytological abnormalities or histologically confirmed cervical cancer. Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) was the most common abnormality, accounting for 70.9% of abnormal cases. HPV DNA was detected in 47.0% of women with normal cytology and 80.0% of women with abnormal cytology ( p < 0.05). Genotyping analysis revealed HPV16 as the predominant high-risk genotype in both women with normal cytology and those with cervical cancer. Multiple HPV genotype infections were common, occurring in 49.1% of HPV-positive participants with normal cytology and 59.5% of cervical cancer cases. In addition to HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, HPV58, and HPV59 were among the most frequently detected high-risk genotypes. This hospital-based cross-sectional study provides insights into the distribution of high-risk HPV genotypes among women with normal cytology and cervical cancer in Mysore, India. HPV16 was the predominant genotype in both groups, with multiple HPV infections observed in majority of study participants. These findings contribute to the understanding of regional HPV genotype distribution and recommend the optimization of HPV-based screening strategies and vaccination programs for better outcomes.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 宫颈癌在印度仍是一项主要的公共卫生负担,持续感染高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)被公认为其主要病因。了解高危型HPV基因型的分布对于优化筛查与抗病毒药物治疗策略至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本院基于社区的横断面研究收集了印度卡纳塔克邦迈索尔三级医院就诊的20–75岁172名非孕女性的宫颈阴道灌洗(CVL)样本。在172名参与者中,117人(68.0%)细胞学检查正常,而55人(32.0%)出现细胞学异常或组织学确诊的宫颈癌。
elements_zh.methods: 通过 MY09/MY11 聚合酶链式反应 (PCR) 检测 HPV DNA,并使用 TRUPCR ® HR-HPV 基因分型试剂盒对 HPV 阳性参与者进行基因分型,该试剂盒可检测 14 种 高危型HPV 基因型。使用巴氏(Pap)试验进行细胞学评估。

title_zh: 印度迈索尔一家医院开展的高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HR-HPV)基因型分布研究:涉及细胞学正常女性及宫颈癌前病变的横断面调查
source_body_en: Cervical cancer remains a major public health burden in India, with persistent infection by high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) recognized as the primary etiological factor. Understanding the distribution of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) genotypes is essential for optimizing screening and vaccination strategies. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence and genotype distribution of HR-HPV among women aged 20–75 years attending tertiary care hospitals in Mysore, Karnataka, India. In this hospital-based cross-sectional study, cervicovaginal lavage (CVL) samples were collected from 172 non-pregnant women aged 20–75 years attending the Obstetrics and Gynecology Departments of JSS Hospital and Cheluvamba Hospital, or the Oncology Department of Krishnarajendra Hospital, Mysore, between August 2021 and March 2023. Cheluvamba hospital and Krishnarajendra hospital belongs to Mysore Medical College and Research Institute (MMCRI), Govt of Karnataka, Karnataka, India. Cytological evaluation was performed using the Papanicolaou (Pap) test. HPV DNA was detected by MY09/MY11 polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and HPV-positive participants were genotyped using the TRUPCR ® HR-HPV Genotyping Kit, which detects 14 high-risk HPV genotypes. Of the 172 participants, 117 (68.0%) had normal cytology, while 55 (32.0%) presented with cytological abnormalities or histologically confirmed cervical cancer. Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) was the most common abnormality, accounting for 70.9% of abnormal cases. HPV DNA was detected in 47.0% of women with normal cytology and 80.0% of women with abnormal cytology ( p < 0.05). Genotyping analysis revealed HPV16 as the predominant high-risk genotype in both women with normal cytology and those with cervical cancer. Multiple HPV genotype infections were common, occurring in 49.1% of HPV-positive participants with normal cytology and 59.5% of cervical cancer cases. In addition to HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, HPV58, and HPV59 were among the most frequently detected high-risk genotypes. This hospital-based cross-sectional study provides insights into the distribution of high-risk HPV genotypes among women with normal cytology and cervical cancer in Mysore, India. HPV16 was the predominant genotype in both groups, with multiple HPV infections observed in majority of study participants. These findings contribute to the understanding of regional HPV genotype distribution and recommend the optimization of HPV-based screening strategies and vaccination programs for better outcomes.

title: Scaling Adolescent Immunity: Multi-Age Cohort Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination Campaigns in West Africa—Evidence from Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Liberia, and Sierra Leone
abstract: Background: Cervical cancer remains a major public health problem, causing approximately 660,000 new cases and 348,000 deaths annually, with more than 90% occurring in low- and middle-income countries. The WHO African Region accounts for approximately 20% of global cases and 30% of deaths. In November 2020, the World Health Assembly adopted the Global Strategy for Cervical Cancer Elimination with 90–70–90 targets for 2030. Multi-age cohort (MAC) campaigns have emerged as a high-impact strategy for achieving population-level HPV vaccination coverage. This study documents the implementation and outcomes of HPV MAC campaigns across Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Liberia, and Sierra Leone in 2025. Methods: This multi-country mixed-methods analysis integrated quantitative administrative campaign data with qualitative programmatic assessments across eight operational readiness domains from the WHO Immunization Readiness Assessment Tool. Data were collected between January and December 2025 from national reports, WHO supervision missions, and partner reports. Coverage analysis used administrative data triangulated with independent monitoring. Equity analysis used school enrolment data and geographic accessibility indices. Results: The campaigns targeted 7,376,096 girls aged 9–18 years and reached approximately 6,306,294, achieving 85.5% overall coverage. Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone reported administrative coverage of 88.0%, 84.5%, 60.0% and 100%, respectively. All four countries achieved the minimum operational readiness threshold of 80% across all assessed domains. A total of 35,860 health workers were trained, with post-training competency scores increasing from 58.8% to 89.5%. Cold chain functionality exceeded 98% across all campaigns. A total of 314 cases of Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFIs) were reported, all classified as mild, giving an approximate rate of 5.0 per 100,000 doses. Coverage gaps between in-school and out-of-school girls ranged from 18 to 35 percentage points. Conclusions: The findings suggest that large-scale adolescent HPV immunization can be successfully implemented in resource-limited settings when supported by political commitment, multisectoral coordination and adequate operational resources. The single-dose schedule transition under Gavi 6.0 offers opportunities to simplify delivery. Priority actions include integrating HPV into routine immunization, scaling equity strategies for out-of-school girls and ensuring sustainable financing.

abstract_zh: 背景:宫颈癌 仍然是一个重大的公共卫生问题,每年造成约 660,000 例新病例和 348,000 例死亡,其中 90% 以上发生在低收入和中等收入国家。世卫组织非洲区域约占全球病例的 20% 和死亡人数的 30%。2020 年 11 月,世界卫生大会通过了 宫颈癌 消除全球战略,其中包括 2030 年 90-70-90 个目标。多年龄段 队列研究 (MAC) 运动已成为实现人口水平 HPV 疫苗接种 覆盖的高影响力战略。本研究记录了 2025 年科特迪瓦、加纳、利比里亚和塞拉利昂 HPV MAC 运动的实施情况和成果。方法:这项多国混合方法分析将定量管理运动数据与世卫组织免疫准备情况评估工具中八个业务准备领域的定性规划评估相结合。数据是在 2025 年 1 月至 12 月期间从国家报告、世卫组织监督任务和合作伙伴报告中收集的。覆盖率分析使用通过独立监测进行三角测量的行政数据。公平分析使用学校入学数据和地理可达性指数。结果:活动针对 7,376,096 名 9-18 岁女孩,覆盖人数约为 6,306,294 人,总体覆盖率达 85.5%。科特迪瓦、加纳、利比里亚和塞拉利昂的行政覆盖率分别为 88.0%、84.5%、60.0% 和 100%。所有四个国家在所有评估领域均达到了 80% 的最低战备状态阈值。累计培训卫生技术人员35860人次,培训后能力得分由58.8%提高到89.5%。所有活动中的冷链功能均超过 98%。总共报告了 314 例免疫接种后不良事件 (AEFI),全部分类为轻度,每 100,000 剂疫苗中大约有 5.0 例。在校女童和失学女童之间的覆盖率差距为 18 至 35 个百分点。结论:研究结果表明,在政治承诺、多部门协调和充足的运营资源的支持下,大规模青少年 HPV 免疫接种可以在资源有限的环境中成功实施。Gavi 6.0 下的单剂量时间表过渡提供了简化给药的机会。优先行动包括将 HPV 纳入常规免疫接种、扩大失学女童的公平战略以​​及确保可持续融资。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 宫颈癌 仍是一项重大公共卫生问题,每年导致约 660,000 例新发病例和 348,000 例死亡,其中 90% 以上发生在中低收入国家。本研究记录了 2025 年在科特迪瓦、加纳、利比里亚和塞拉利昂开展的 HPV 多年龄层 队列研究 疫苗接种运动的实施情况及结果。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 多年龄段 队列研究 (MAC) 活动已成为实现人群水平 HPV 疫苗接种 覆盖的高影响力策略。该活动针对 7,376,096 名 9-18 岁女孩,覆盖人数约 6,306,294 人,总体覆盖率达到 85.5%。
analysis_zh.methods: 数据收集时间为2025年1月至12月,来源包括国家报告、世界卫生组织督导任务及合作伙伴报告。覆盖率分析采用行政数据与独立监测的三角验证。公平性分析使用学校入学数据和地理可及性指数。
analysis_zh.main_results: 科特迪瓦、加纳、利比里亚和塞拉利昂报告的行政覆盖率分别为88.0%、84.5%、60.0%和100%。四国在所有评估领域均达到最低80%运行就绪阈值。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在政治承诺、多部门协调和充足的运营资源的支持下,大规模青少年 HPV 免疫接种可以在资源有限的环境中成功实施。Gavi 6.0 下的单剂量时间表过渡提供了简化给药的机会。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为在资源有限的环境中实施大规模青少年 HPV 免疫的可行性提供了证据,这可以为未来的 疫苗接种 策略和公共卫生干预措施提供信息。优先行动包括将 HPV 纳入常规免疫接种、扩大失学女童的公平战略以​​及确保可持续融资。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究设计的具体限制。该研究提供了多个国家的详细覆盖范围和运营准备数据,因此证据强度很高。

title: Parental knowledge, attitude and acceptability of Human Papillomavirus vaccine: implications for the prevention of cervical cancer in India
abstract: Abstract The Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is a key tool for cervical cancer prevention; however, vaccine uptake in India remains low despite its recent introduction as a free single-dose vaccine through the public health system. Parental acceptance to vaccination is key to ensure vaccine uptake of adolescent girls. Hence, this study was conducted to assess the knowledge, attitude and acceptability of HPV vaccination parents of adolescent girls, during the early phase of HPV vaccine rollout. This community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 422 parents of adolescent girls, during the early phase of HPV vaccine rollout in the country, to assess their knowledge, attitude and acceptability of HPV vaccination. Only 18.2% of participants had heard of HPV infection, 6.6% identified HPV as the primary cause of cervical cancer, and 8.5% had heard of the HPV vaccine, with only 5.9% demonstrated good knowledge of vaccination. Despite limited knowledge, 48.8% had a positive attitude, 62.6% demonstrated good acceptability, and 72.7% expressed willingness for vaccination. Higher parental education and healthcare-related occupations were associated with greater vaccine acceptability in bivariate analysis. Significant positive correlations were observed among knowledge of HPV infection and cervical cancer, HPV vaccine knowledge, attitudes, and vaccine acceptability ( p < 0.001). These findings highlight persistent knowledge gaps despite moderate-to-high acceptability. Targeted interventions using community health workers (ASHAs) and digital platforms are needed to improve informed decision-making and support equitable HPV vaccine uptake in disadvantaged settings, contributing to India’s cervical cancer elimination goals.

HPV vaccination is a highly effective and safe primary prevention intervention; however, uptake of vaccination programs is strongly influenced by the level of knowledge and perceptions of the target population, particularly among adolescents. In this context, educational interventions at schools play a central role in promoting awareness and favorable attitudes toward preventive behaviors. Materials and Methods. The study involved a sample of 2,146 students attending first and second grade secondary schools in the 3 Wester Sicily provinces of Agrigento, Palermo and Trapani. source_records.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted infection and is associated with the development of several diseases, including malignancies such as cervical, anal, vulvar, vaginal penile, oropharyngeal cancers and benign lesions such as genital warts. HPV vaccination is a highly effective and safe primary prevention intervention; however, uptake of vaccination programs is strongly influenced by the level of knowledge and perceptions of the target population, particularly among adolescents. In this context, educational interventions at schools play a central role in promoting awareness and favorable attitudes toward preventive behaviors. Materials and Methods. The study involved a sample of 2,146 students attending first and second grade secondary schools in the 3 Wester Sicily provinces of Agrigento, Palermo and Trapani. Participants were involved via the administration of a structured questionnaire designed to assess their knowledge, attitudes toward HPV and its vaccination, and willingness to receive vaccination. A second version of the questionnaire was re-administered following training sessions aimed to providing scientific information on the infection and prevention strategies. Responses were collected using Likert scales ranging from 1 to 5 to assess opinions and from 1 to 10 to measure vaccination willingness. Participation in the study required a written informed consent previously signed from the students' parents. Students showed a high level of agreement with the statement that the virus can cause serious illness, with an average score of 4.5 out of 5, and acknowledged the possibility of being exposed to the infection during their lifetime, with an average score of 3.9. A strong perception of the importance of communication on the topic also emerged, both within the family, school, and healthcare settings, with average scores of 4.23, 4.46, and 4.21, respectively. Regarding the Vaccination, participants expressed a high level of agreement regarding the vaccine's usefulness in preventing cervical cancer and genital warts (mean 4.5), its safety (mean 4.32), and the appropriateness of their peers getting vaccinated (mean 4.48). analysis.methods: Participants completed a structured questionnaire to assess their knowledge, attitudes, and willingness to accept HPV vaccination, with a second version administered after training sessions to provide scientific information.
analysis.main_results: Students showed high agreement with the statement that HPV can cause serious illness (mean score 4.5) and acknowledged lifetime exposure risk (mean score 3.9). Vaccination willingness increased from 8.62 to 8.94 on a 1-10 scale (p-value < 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that educational interventions can enhance students' understanding and willingness to accept HPV vaccination, particularly regarding its role in preventing cervical cancer and genital warts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that targeted educational efforts in schools could improve HPV vaccination uptake, contributing to public health strategies aimed at reducing HPV-related diseases.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the knowledge, attitudes, and willingness to accept human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination among 2,146 students in Western Sicily. It found that students had a high level of agreement regarding HPV's association with serious illnesses and its prevention through vaccination. Educational interventions significantly increased vaccination willingness, with a mean score rising from 8.62 to 8.94 on a 1-10 scale. The study highlights the importance of school-based education in promoting HPV vaccination, particularly for preventing cervical cancer and genital warts. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and its focus on a single population may limit the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is strong, as it includes structured questionnaires and statistical analysis, but further research is needed to confirm these results in broader contexts.

title: High-risk HPV detection via GeneXpert in self-collected anal swabs among MSM living with HIV: Insights from a cross-sectional study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Men who have sex with men living with HIV (MSMLWHIV) have a high risk of persistent high-risk HPV infection, and rapid tools like Xpert HPV can help expand screening in low-resource settings. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the feasibility of using self-collected anal swabs for detecting high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infections in MSMLWHIV, using the Xpert® HPV assay. Additionally, we investigated factors associated with HR-HPV positivity. DESIGN: This was a single-center cross-sectional study conducted from 22nd May 2024 to 31st July 2024 among MSMLWHIV in Bamako. METHODS: Participants were recruited from the Soutoura NGO in Bamako, Mali. To be eligible, individuals had to be HIV-1 positive, on antiretroviral therapy, 18 years or older, and self-identified as MSM. The prevalence of HR-HPV was reported by sociodemographic characteristics and sexual behaviors. We used a penalized logistic regression model using Firth's method to identify sociodemographic and behavioral factors associated with HR-HPV positivity. RESULTS: A total of 245 MSMLWHIV were initially tested. Of these, 170 yielded successful results and were subsequently included in the study analysis. The participants had a median age of 26 years (IQR 24-29) with the median age of first anal intercourse at 16 years (IQR 16-18). Among the participants, 29% (49/170) identified as bisexual, 42% (72/170) reported never using condoms, 16% (27/170) participated in group intercourse, and 42% (71/170) had at least two different sexual partners in the past six months. Among those successfully tested, 65% (110/170) were positive for HR-HPV, with HPV16 detected in 12% (21/170) of participants. No or primary education and consistent condom use were associated with lower odds of HR-HPV positivity, while the unexpected association observed with smoking should be interpreted with caution. CONCLUSION: The high HR-HPV prevalence among MSMLWHIV calls for targeted screening and prevention. Although Xpert HPV shows promise, the 31% failure rate with self-collected samples underscores the need for improvements in sample collection procedures and technical performance.

analysis_zh.main_results: 最初测试了总共 245 名 MSMLWHIV。其中,170 个取得了成功的结果,随后被纳入研究分析。在成功检测的参与者中,65% (110/170) 的 HR-HPV 呈阳性,其中 12% (21/170) 的参与者检测到 HPV16。未受过教育或接受过初等教育以及持续使用安全套与 HR-HPV 阳性的几率较低有关,而观察到的与吸烟的意外关联应谨慎解释。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: MSMLWHIV 中 HR-HPV 患病率 较高,呼吁有针对性的筛查和预防。尽管 Xpert HPV 显示出前景,但自行采集样本 31% 的失败率凸显了样本采集程序和技术性能需要改进。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了针对 MSMLWHIV 中 HR-HPV 进行针对性筛查的重要性,并表明需要改进样本采集方法,以提高自我采集肛门拭子用于 HPV 检测的可靠性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在单个中心进行的,这可能会限制普遍性。自行采集样本的失败率为 31%,表明 Xpert HPV 检测在该人群中的技术性能存在潜在局限性。

title: Atomic resolution structure of human papillomavirus bound to heparin
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a significant health burden and leading cause of virus-induced cancers. The mechanisms of HPV receptor binding and host entry are not completely understood, although it is known that heparan sulfate proteoglycans (HSPGs) mediate entry. HPV16 quasivirus, composed of L1 and L2 capsid proteins with a packaged cottontail rabbit papillomavirus genome was incubated with heparin. The complex was vitrified, and data were collected for cryoEM single particle analysis. Subparticles were extracted and hexavalent and pentavalent capsomers were refined separately. Here we present the resulting 1.9 Å resolution structure, with heparin visualized around the capsomer at the icosahedral fivefold vertex. A model of the asymmetric unit was built unambiguously into the atomic resolution cryoEM map. Hydrogen bonds are predicted between L1 N-terminal regions, which are supported by molecular dynamics. The heparin binding site was identified, along with local L1 conformational changes and global flexibility changes. These changes induced by heparin binding likely reflect the structure of HPV during early stages of entry and provide a framework for future HPV biochemical, genetic, and biophysical studies. Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a significant health burden, but the mechanisms of HPV receptor binding are not understood. Here, the authors solve a 1.9 Å resolution structure of HPV bound to heparin with insights into the binding interface.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the incomplete understanding of human papillomavirus (HPV) receptor binding and host entry mechanisms, particularly the role of heparan sulfate proteoglycans (HSPGs) in mediating entry.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors used HPV16 quasivirus composed of L1 and L2 capsid proteins with a packaged cottontail rabbit papillomavirus genome, incubated with heparin, and analyzed by cryoEM single particle analysis.
analysis.methods: HPV16 quasivirus was incubated with heparin, vitrified, and subjected to cryoEM single particle analysis to obtain a 1.9 Å resolution structure, with subparticles extracted and capsomers refined separately.
analysis.main_results: The resulting 1.9 Å resolution structure visualized heparin bound around the capsomer at the icosahedral fivefold vertex, with a model of the asymmetric unit built unambiguously into the atomic resolution cryoEM map.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The heparin binding site was identified, along with local L1 conformational changes and global flexibility changes, likely reflecting the structure of HPV during early stages of entry and providing a framework for future studies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The atomic-resolution structure of HPV bound to heparin advances mechanistic understanding of HPV entry, informing future biochemical, genetic, and biophysical studies relevant to HPV biology and potential therapeutic targeting.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to structural analysis of HPV16 quasivirus in vitro with heparin, and the evidence strength is high due to the atomic resolution achieved but remains constrained by the absence of in vivo validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study resolves the 1.9 Å cryoEM structure of HPV16 quasivirus bound to heparin, revealing the heparin binding site at the icosahedral fivefold vertex and associated L1 conformational changes. The atomic-resolution map enables unambiguous modeling of the asymmetric unit, providing mechanistic insights into early HPV entry events. These findings establish a structural framework for future HPV research, though the study is limited to in vitro analysis and lacks in vivo validation.

title: A Cell-Penetrating Peptide and Signal Sequence Fusion DNA Vaccine Enhances CD8+ T Cell-Mediated Anti-Tumor Immunity Targeting HPV-16 Cervical Cancer Antigens.
abstract: Background Cervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer affecting women, with almost all cases caused by infection with Human Papillomavirus (HPV). Previous research has explored the potential of cell-penetrating peptides to improve the efficacy of peptide vaccines and signal peptide sequences to increase protein secretion in DNA vaccines. In this study, we evaluated the in vivo efficacy of DNA vaccines targeting HPV-16 E6 and E7 viral antigens that are constructed with both a cell-penetrating peptide and IL-2 signal peptide to improve immunogenicity. Results We generated DNA vaccine constructs utilizing combinations of E7(49-57), E6(48-57), IL-2 signal sequence (sig), 9-polyarginine (9R), and 12-polyarginine (12R) cloned into pcDNA3 vectors. Transfection of the pcDNA3-sig9RE7, pcDNA3-sig12RE7, or pcDNA3-9RE7 vaccine constructs induced a significant E7-specific CD8+ T cell response in vitro. We observed that the pcDNA3-sig9RE7 vaccine induced the strongest E7-specific immune response in vivo compared to the pcDNA3-9RE7 and pcDNA3-sig12RE7 constructs. We demonstrated the potential protective and therapeutic anti-tumor effects of the pcDNA3-sig9RE7 vaccination against the HPV-16 E7 expressing TC-1 tumor model in mice. Finally, we found similar anti-tumor effects for the pcDNA3-sig9RE6 vaccine which suggest this DNA vaccine strategy could be applied to various cervical cancer antigens. Conclusion Treatment with the pcDNA3-sig9RE7 DNA vaccine induces a potent E7-specific anti-tumor immune response in mice. By demonstrating the potential of utilizing a cell-penetrating peptide and signal peptide sequence in combination to improve efficacy, this study provides a foundation for future research into fusion DNA vaccines with cell-penetrating peptides and signal peptide combinations.

title_zh: 一种细胞穿透肽与信号肽融合DNA 疫苗可增强针对HPV-16 宫颈癌抗原的CD8+ T细胞介导的抗肿瘤免疫
source_body_en: Background Cervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer affecting women, with almost all cases caused by infection with Human Papillomavirus (HPV). Previous research has explored the potential of cell-penetrating peptides to improve the efficacy of peptide vaccines and signal peptide sequences to increase protein secretion in DNA vaccines. In this study, we evaluated the in vivo efficacy of DNA vaccines targeting HPV-16 E6 and E7 viral antigens that are constructed with both a cell-penetrating peptide and IL-2 signal peptide to improve immunogenicity. Results We generated DNA vaccine constructs utilizing combinations of E7(49-57), E6(48-57), IL-2 signal sequence (sig), 9-polyarginine (9R), and 12-polyarginine (12R) cloned into pcDNA3 vectors. Transfection of the pcDNA3-sig9RE7, pcDNA3-sig12RE7, or pcDNA3-9RE7 vaccine constructs induced a significant E7-specific CD8+ T cell response in vitro. We observed that the pcDNA3-sig9RE7 vaccine induced the strongest E7-specific immune response in vivo compared to the pcDNA3-9RE7 and pcDNA3-sig12RE7 constructs. We demonstrated the potential protective and therapeutic anti-tumor effects of the pcDNA3-sig9RE7 vaccination against the HPV-16 E7 expressing TC-1 tumor model in mice. Finally, we found similar anti-tumor effects for the pcDNA3-sig9RE6 vaccine which suggest this DNA vaccine strategy could be applied to various cervical cancer antigens. Conclusion Treatment with the pcDNA3-sig9RE7 DNA vaccine induces a potent E7-specific anti-tumor immune response in mice. By demonstrating the potential of utilizing a cell-penetrating peptide and signal peptide sequence in combination to improve efficacy, this study provides a foundation for future research into fusion DNA vaccines with cell-penetrating peptides and signal peptide combinations.
abstract_zh: 背景 宫颈癌是女性第四常见癌症,几乎所有病例均由感染人乳头瘤病毒(人乳头瘤病毒,HPV)引起。早期研究已探索细胞穿透肽在提升肽疫苗疗效及信号肽在增强DNA 疫苗蛋白分泌中的潜力。本研究评估了靶向HPV-16 E6和E7病毒抗原的DNA 疫苗在体内疗效,该DNA构建了细胞穿透肽与IL-2信号肽融合以提高免疫原性。结果 我们构建了多种DNA 疫苗载体,包括E7(49-57)、E6(48-57)、IL-2信号序列(sig)、9-聚精氨酸(9R)及12-聚精氨酸(12R),并将其克隆至pcDNA3 媒介载体。转染pcDNA3-sig9RE7、pcDNA3-sig12RE7或pcDNA3-9RE7 疫苗载体后,体外可诱导显著的E7特异性CD8+ T细胞应答。研究发现,与pcDNA3-9RE7及pcDNA3-sig12RE7载体相比,pcDNA3-sig9RE7 疫苗在体内诱导了最强的E7特异性免疫应答。我们证明了pcDNA3-sig9RE7 疫苗在小鼠HPV-16 E7表达TC-1肿瘤模型中具有潜在的保护性及治疗性抗肿瘤效应。最后,我们发现pcDNA3-sig9RE6 疫苗同样具有类似的抗肿瘤效应,提示该DNA 疫苗策略可应用于多种宫颈癌抗原。结论 治疗与pcDNA3-sig9RE7 DNA 疫苗在小鼠体内可诱导强效E7特异性抗肿瘤免疫应答。通过展示细胞穿透肽与信号肽序列联合应用以提升疗效的潜力,本研究为未来融合DNA 疫苗与细胞穿透肽及信号肽组合的研究奠定了基础。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 宫颈癌 是影响女性的第四大常见癌症,几乎所有病例都是由 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染引起。先前的研究探索了细胞穿透肽提高肽 疫苗 功效的潜力,以及信号肽序列增加 DNA 疫苗 中蛋白质分泌的潜力。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这项研究中,我们评估了 DNA 疫苗 靶向 HPV-16 E6 和 E7 病毒抗原的体内功效,这些抗原由细胞穿透肽和 IL-2 信号肽构建,以提高免疫原性。
analysis_zh.methods: 我们利用克隆到 pcDNA3 媒介 中的 E7(49-57)、E6(48-57)、IL-2 信号序列 (sig)、9-聚精氨酸 (9R) 和 12-聚精氨酸 (12R) 的组合生成 DNA 疫苗 构建体。
analysis_zh.main_results: pcDNA3-sig9RE7、pcDNA3-sig12RE7 或 pcDNA3-9RE7 疫苗 构建体的转染在体外诱导显着的 E7 特异性 CD8+ T 细胞反应。我们观察到,与 pcDNA3-9RE7 和 pcDNA3-sig12RE7 构建体相比,pcDNA3-sig9RE7 疫苗 在体内诱导最强的 E7 特异性 免疫应答。我们证明了 pcDNA3-sig9RE7 疫苗接种 对小鼠中表达 HPV-16 E7 的 TC-1 肿瘤模型的潜在保护和治疗性抗肿瘤作用。最后,我们发现 pcDNA3-sig9RE6 疫苗 具有类似的抗肿瘤作用,这表明该 DNA 疫苗 策略可以应用于各种 宫颈癌 抗原。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 治疗与pcDNA3-sig9RE7 DNA 疫苗在小鼠体内可诱导强效E7特异性抗肿瘤免疫应答。通过展示细胞穿透肽与信号肽序列联合应用以提升疗效的潜力,本研究为未来融合DNA 疫苗与细胞穿透肽及信号肽组合的研究奠定了基础。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究为融合DNA 疫苗与细胞穿透肽及信号肽组合的未来研究奠定了基础,该策略有望增强针对HPV相关宫颈癌的免疫原性及抗肿瘤免疫。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据未报告本研究的局限性。

title: Coreactant-specific electrochemiluminescence of an anthracene-based zinc framework for detection of HPV-16 DNA.
abstract: The efficient activation of a coreactant is challenging in electrochemiluminescence (ECL) enhancement. Herein, a metal-organic framework nanoemitter was designed with an anthracene derivative as a luminophore ligand and a Zn 2+ node. It demonstrated a 1,4-diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane (DABCO)-specific ECL pathway via coordination interaction between the coreactant and the Zn 2+ node, which significantly enhanced emission over conventional coreactants, establishing a sensitive strategy for DNA detection.

title: Long-term risk of cancer following cervical intraepithelial neoplasia: A significant study leveraging Taiwan's national health insurance research database
abstract: OBJECTIVES: We used Taiwan's national health insurance research database to conduct a study on the risk of cancer after cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study analyzed data from the Taiwan NHIRD comparing three cohorts: one with precancerous cervical dysplasia (CIN2+ dysplasia), one with mild dysplasia or undetermined dysplasia (non-CIN2+ dysplasia), and one without dysplasia. We excluded patients with index dates before 2001 or after 2016 and adjusted factors to analyze future cancer risks. RESULTS: There were 776, 1248, and 14,421 new cases in the CIN2+ cohort, non-CIN2+ cohort, and cohort without cervical dysplasia, respectively. The competing hazard ratios (95% CI) for the risk of all cancer, cervical or endocervical cancer, malignancy of the anogenital tract, head and neck cancer, respiratory cancer, breast cancer, ovary or uterus cancer, and colon cancer in the CIN2+ and non-CIN2+ cohorts were 2.312 (2.112-2.53) and 1.195 (1.104-1.293), 15.518 (11.936-20.175) and 6.045 (4.713-7.754), 9.369 (4.022-21.821) and 4.451 (2.01-9.856), 2.328 (1.446-3.746) and 1.111 (0.707-1.746), 2.125 (1.622-2.783) and 1.147 (0.896-1.467), 1.794 (1.492-2.158) and 0.98 (0.843-1.139), 0.786 (0.45-1.372) and 1.375 (1.055-1.793), 2.315 (1.832-2.927) and 1.114 (0.885-1.401), respectively. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that moderate or severe cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and carcinoma in situ significantly increase long-term cancer risk, even after surgical intervention. Patients with a history of mild or undetermined cervical dysplasia also face heightened cancer risk, emphasizing the need for consistent monitoring.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the long-term risk of cancer following cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, addressing the need to understand the association between precancerous lesions and subsequent malignancies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used Taiwan's national health insurance research database to compare three cohorts: those with precancerous cervical dysplasia (CIN2+ dysplasia), those with mild dysplasia or undetermined dysplasia (non-CIN2+ dysplasia), and those without dysplasia. The analysis included 776, 1248, and 14,421 new cases in these cohorts, respectively.
analysis.methods: The study excluded patients with index dates before 2001 or after 2016 and adjusted for various factors to analyze future cancer risks. It used competing hazard ratios to assess the risk of different cancer types across the cohorts.
analysis.main_results: The competing hazard ratios (95% CI) for cancer risk were 2.312 (2.112-2.53) for the CIN2+ cohort and 1.195 (1.104-1.293) for the non-CIN2+ cohort, with significant differences observed for several cancer types.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that moderate or severe cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and carcinoma in situ significantly increase long-term cancer risk, even after surgical intervention, highlighting the importance of ongoing monitoring.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize the need for consistent surveillance and management of patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia to mitigate long-term cancer risks, particularly for high-risk HPV-related malignancies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a national health insurance database, which may have biases or missing data, and the evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study leveraged Taiwan's national health insurance research database to examine the long-term cancer risk following cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. It compared three cohorts: those with moderate or severe dysplasia (CIN2+), those with mild or undetermined dysplasia (non-CIN2+), and those without dysplasia. The results showed significantly elevated cancer risks in the CIN2+ cohort compared to the non-CIN2+ and control groups, with hazard ratios indicating a higher likelihood of various cancers, including cervical, anogenital, and head and neck cancers. The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that even after surgical intervention, CIN2+ and carcinoma in situ are associated with increased cancer risk, underscoring the importance of continued monitoring. The study's evidence is moderate due to its observational design and potential database limitations, but it provides valuable insights into the long-term implications of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia for cancer surveillance and management.

title_zh: 宫颈上皮内瘤变后长期癌症风险:一项利用台湾国家健康保险研究数据库的重要研究
source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: We used Taiwan's national health insurance research database to conduct a study on the risk of cancer after cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study analyzed data from the Taiwan NHIRD comparing three cohorts: one with precancerous cervical dysplasia (CIN2+ dysplasia), one with mild dysplasia or undetermined dysplasia (non-CIN2+ dysplasia), and one without dysplasia. We excluded patients with index dates before 2001 or after 2016 and adjusted factors to analyze future cancer risks. RESULTS: There were 776, 1248, and 14,421 new cases in the CIN2+ cohort, non-CIN2+ cohort, and cohort without cervical dysplasia, respectively. The competing hazard ratios (95% CI) for the risk of all cancer, cervical or endocervical cancer, malignancy of the anogenital tract, head and neck cancer, respiratory cancer, breast cancer, ovary or uterus cancer, and colon cancer in the CIN2+ and non-CIN2+ cohorts were 2.312 (2.112-2.53) and 1.195 (1.104-1.293), 15.518 (11.936-20.175) and 6.045 (4.713-7.754), 9.369 (4.022-21.821) and 4.451 (2.01-9.856), 2.328 (1.446-3.746) and 1.111 (0.707-1.746), 2.125 (1.622-2.783) and 1.147 (0.896-1.467), 1.794 (1.492-2.158) and 0.98 (0.843-1.139), 0.786 (0.45-1.372) and 1.375 (1.055-1.793), 2.315 (1.832-2.927) and 1.114 (0.885-1.401), respectively. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that moderate or severe cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and carcinoma in situ significantly increase long-term cancer risk, even after surgical intervention. Patients with a history of mild or undetermined cervical dysplasia also face heightened cancer risk, emphasizing the need for consistent monitoring.

title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus in the public health system of the central-northern region of Chile
abstract: OBJECTIVE Previously, we found a high prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the private health system. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the frequency of HR-HPV in a large cohort of women attending the public health system and to compare these findings. METHODS A total of 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique. RESULTS The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection between 2020 and 2024 was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with annual values of 13.07%, 12.64%, 14.80%, 14.24%, and 14.15% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. In women under 25 years of age, the prevalence of HR-HPV was 34.03% during the evaluated period, compared to 16.35% in women aged 25 to 44 years, 10.47% in those aged 45 to 64 years, and 11.52% in women over 64 years of age. Pap smears showed 89.71% NILM results in HPV-negative women, compared to 74.59% in HPV-positive women. The rates of LSIL and HSIL were 0.14% and 0.07% in HPV-negative women, respectively; however, these values increased to 4.73% and 4.43% in HPV-positive women, respectively. Probable carcinoma was found in only 0.006% of HPV-negative women, but in 0.46% of HPV-positive women. CONCLUSIONS The prevalence of HR-HPV infection in women attending the public health system in the central-northern region appears to be similar to that previously reported in Chile, but lower than that reported in the same region for women attending the private health system.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to determine the frequency of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the public health system, as previous research had found a high prevalence in the private health system.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study analyzed 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 in the central-northern region of Chile.
analysis.methods: Samples were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique to detect HR-HPV infection and cytological abnormalities.
analysis.main_results: The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with higher rates in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older age groups. HPV-positive women had markedly increased rates of cytological abnormalities, including LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) compared to HPV-negative women. These findings provide valuable data for public health planning and targeted screening programs.

title_zh: 智利中北部地区公共卫生系统中的患病率 人乳头瘤病毒
source_body_en: OBJECTIVE Previously, we found a high prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the private health system. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the frequency of HR-HPV in a large cohort of women attending the public health system and to compare these findings. METHODS A total of 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique. RESULTS The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection between 2020 and 2024 was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with annual values of 13.07%, 12.64%, 14.80%, 14.24%, and 14.15% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. In women under 25 years of age, the prevalence of HR-HPV was 34.03% during the evaluated period, compared to 16.35% in women aged 25 to 44 years, 10.47% in those aged 45 to 64 years, and 11.52% in women over 64 years of age. Pap smears showed 89.71% NILM results in HPV-negative women, compared to 74.59% in HPV-positive women. The rates of LSIL and HSIL were 0.14% and 0.07% in HPV-negative women, respectively; however, these values increased to 4.73% and 4.43% in HPV-positive women, respectively. Probable carcinoma was found in only 0.006% of HPV-negative women, but in 0.46% of HPV-positive women. CONCLUSIONS The prevalence of HR-HPV infection in women attending the public health system in the central-northern region appears to be similar to that previously reported in Chile, but lower than that reported in the same region for women attending the private health system.

title: Clinicopathological Characteristics and Long-Term Outcomes After Conization for Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia Grade 2 (CIN2)
abstract: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 (CIN2) represents a clinically heterogeneous condition with variable risks of persistence, regression, and progression. This study evaluated the clinicopathological characteristics and long-term outcomes of patients undergoing cervical conization for CIN2 and explored factors associated with residual or recurrent disease. A total of 195 patients treated between July 2016 and February 2026 were included. The median follow-up duration was 1.75 years (IQR, 0.83–5.04 years). Post-conization histology showed that 50.7% of cases were downgraded to CIN1 or normal, 35.8% persisted as CIN2, and 13.3% were upgraded to higher-grade lesions. Negative surgical margins were observed in 88.2% of patients. Findings suggestive of residual disease were identified in 26 patients during early follow-up, although histologically confirmed residual CIN2+ disease was observed in only three cases. During follow-up, nine patients developed findings suggestive for recurrence, whereas histologically confirmed recurrent CIN2+ disease was confirmed in three patients. HPV clearance was observed in 75% of patients with available follow-up testing. Multivariable analysis did not identify any independent predictors of relapse. These findings suggest that most CIN2 lesions regress or remain stable after conization, with low rates of histologically confirmed residual or recurrent high-grade disease, and highlight the limited predictive value of conventional clinicopathological factors in identifying patients at risk of relapse.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估行宫颈锥切术治疗的宫颈上皮内瘤变2级(CIN2)患者的临床病理特征及长期结局,并探索与残留或复发性疾病相关的因素。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究共纳入2016年7月至2026年2月期间接受治疗的195名患者。中位随访时长为1.75年(四分位距,0.83–5.04年)。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究通过锥切术后组织学评估病变的降级、持续及进展情况,并评估手术切缘及随访发现以判断残留或复发性疾病。
analysis_zh.main_results: 锥切术后组织学显示,50.7%的病例降级至CIN1或正常,35.8%持续为CIN2,13.3%进展为高级别病变。88.2%的患者手术切缘为阴性。早期随访中,26例患者出现残留病变的影像学表现,但组织学确认的残留CIN2+病变仅3例。随访期间,9例患者出现复发的影像学表现,而组织学确认的复发性CIN2+病变仅3例。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果提示,大多数CIN2病变在锥切术后退行或保持稳定,高级别残留或复发性疾病的组织学确认率较低,并凸显常规临床病理因素在识别复发风险患者方面的有限预测价值。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为宫颈锥切术后CIN2的自然病程提供了见解,可为HPV相关宫颈疾病的临床决策及监测策略提供参考。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究依赖组织学确认残留或复发性疾病,可能无法涵盖所有病例,证据强度为中等,因研究为观察性设计且存在潜在混杂因素。

title: HPV-associated Anal Dysplasia in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients: A Transplant-specific Model of Mucosal Immune Dysfunction
abstract: ABSTRACT: Solid organ transplant recipients face an increased risk of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated anal cancer because of chronic immunosuppression and impaired viral control. The natural history and underlying biology of anal dysplasia in this population remain poorly defined, and current management is largely extrapolated from human immunodeficiency virus-associated disease. Transplant-related immune dysfunction differs fundamentally from other immunocompromised states, with direct effects on T-cell activation, antigen presentation, and immune memory that are central to HPV control. In this overview, we integrate insights from HPV-driven carcinogenesis, HIV-associated anal disease, and transplant immunology to propose a transplant-specific framework of mucosal immune dysfunction. In this model, HPV immune evasion synergizes chronic immunosuppression to impair antiviral cellular immunity, promoting persistent infection, and a protumorigenic microenvironment characterized by T-cell dysfunction, impaired antigen presentation, regulatory immune polarization, and metabolic reprogramming. These processes are hypothesized to facilitate progression to high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions, the immediate precursor to anal cancer. This framework provides a biologic basis to interpret clinically observed persistence and recurrence of anal dysplasia in solid organ transplant recipients, highlights key knowledge gaps and may inform transplant-specific screening, therapeutic strategies, and prospective studies in this high-risk population.

abstract_zh: 摘要:由于慢性免疫抑制和病毒控制受损,实体器官移植受者患 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 相关肛门癌的风险增加。该人群肛门发育不良的自然史和基础生物学仍不清楚,目前的治疗很大程度上是从人类免疫缺陷病毒相关疾病中推断出来的。移植相关的免疫功能障碍与其他免疫功能低下状态有根本不同,它直接影响对 HPV 控制至关重要的 T 细胞激活、抗原呈递和免疫记忆。在本概述中,我们整合了 HPV 驱动的致癌作用、HIV 相关肛门疾病和移植免疫学的见解,提出了粘膜免疫功能障碍的移植特异性框架。在该模型中,HPV 免疫逃避协同慢性免疫抑制,损害 抗病毒药物 细胞免疫,促进持续感染,以及以 T 细胞功能障碍、抗原呈递受损、调节性免疫极化和代谢重编程为特征的促肿瘤微环境。假设这些过程促进高级鳞状上皮内病变的进展,这是肛门癌的直接前兆。该框架为解释临床观察到的实体器官移植受者肛门发育不良的持续性和复发提供了生物学基础,强调了关键的知识差距,并可能为这一高危人群的移植特异性筛查、治疗策略和前瞻性研究提供信息。

title: HPV-associated Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: An Imaging Framework for AJCC Version 9 TNM Staging
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is biologically and prognostically distinct from HPV-negative disease, and staging directly impacts treatment. The American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) and Union for International Cancer Control version 9 TNM staging system incorporates unequivocal imaging-detected and/or clinically detected extranodal extension (iENE) into clinical nodal staging and definitive pathologic extranodal extension into pathologic nodal staging. Additionally, it provides more explicit anatomic definitions for advanced local disease (clinical T4) while maintaining T and M category definitions from the eighth edition. Radiologists play a central role in the multidisciplinary team by evaluating endophytic tumor extent, regional nodal disease and iENE, and distant metastasis using CT, MRI, and PET. This article reviews clinically relevant oropharyngeal anatomy and proposes a practical radiologic approach to assigning T, N, and M categories in HPV-associated OPSCC. It emphasizes cautious interpretation of iENE because of interreader variability and imperfect diagnostic performance, with further high-grade evidence needed to establish its consistently reproducible, incremental prognostic value as a clinical N category modifier. It also highlights multidisciplinary factors that guide selection of surgical resection versus nonsurgical therapy. Posttreatment evaluation is discussed in the context of blood-based biomarkers such as tumor tissue-modified viral HPV DNA. The goal of this article is to provide a practical, staging-focused imaging framework for evaluation of HPV-associated OPSCC. Keywords: CT, MR Imaging, Head/Neck, Neck, Pharynx, Surgery, Human Papillomavirus, Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Oropharynx, Transoral Robotic Surgery, Oropharyngeal Carcinoma, TTMV HPV DNA © RSNA, 2026.

title_zh: HPV 相关口咽鳞状细胞癌:AJCC 第 9 版 TNM 分期的影像框架
source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is biologically and prognostically distinct from HPV-negative disease, and staging directly impacts treatment. The American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) and Union for International Cancer Control version 9 TNM staging system incorporates unequivocal imaging-detected and/or clinically detected extranodal extension (iENE) into clinical nodal staging and definitive pathologic extranodal extension into pathologic nodal staging. Additionally, it provides more explicit anatomic definitions for advanced local disease (clinical T4) while maintaining T and M category definitions from the eighth edition. Radiologists play a central role in the multidisciplinary team by evaluating endophytic tumor extent, regional nodal disease and iENE, and distant metastasis using CT, MRI, and PET. This article reviews clinically relevant oropharyngeal anatomy and proposes a practical radiologic approach to assigning T, N, and M categories in HPV-associated OPSCC. It emphasizes cautious interpretation of iENE because of interreader variability and imperfect diagnostic performance, with further high-grade evidence needed to establish its consistently reproducible, incremental prognostic value as a clinical N category modifier. It also highlights multidisciplinary factors that guide selection of surgical resection versus nonsurgical therapy. Posttreatment evaluation is discussed in the context of blood-based biomarkers such as tumor tissue-modified viral HPV DNA. The goal of this article is to provide a practical, staging-focused imaging framework for evaluation of HPV-associated OPSCC. title: Efficacy of mRNA-based HPV Vaccines in Inducing Immune Response and Preventing Oncogenic Outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection represents a substantial global health burden, being the primary etiological agent of cervical cancer, anogenital and oropharyngeal malignancies. Although prophylactic virus-like particle (VLP) vaccines have been successfully implemented, they lack therapeutic efficacy against established infections and lesions in the host. The messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccine platform has emerged as a promising alternative, offering rapid manufacturing and the ability to induce potent cellular immune responses required for effective therapeutic outcomes. Objective This systematic review aimed to synthesize and evaluate preclinical evidence regarding the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of mRNA-based HPV vaccines in animal models, focusing on their ability to prevent oncogenic infections and induce regression of established tumors. Methods The study is registered in Prospero (CRD420261362037, 14 July 2026). A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Europe PMC, and ScienceDirect databases was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies included in vivo preclinical experimental research evaluating mRNA vaccines targeting high-risk HPV types (HPV-16 and HPV-18) in animal models. Immunogenicity (CD8+ T-cell responses and IgG titers) and oncogenic outcome (tumor volume and survival rate) data were extracted. The risk of bias was assessed using the SYRCLE’s risk-of-bias tool. The meta-analysis utilized a random-effects model to calculate standardized mean differences (SMD) and evaluate heterogeneity via the I 2 statistic. Result and Conclusion Ten studies met the inclusion criteria and provided detailed data for the analysis. mRNA vaccines have demonstrated high immunogenicity, significantly expanding antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell populations and inducing robust IFN gamma secretion. The pooled results indicated a significant reduction in tumor volume (SMD -2.305; 95% CI: −2.64 to −1.97) and near-complete viral load reduction in the challenge models. High-risk HPV mRNA vaccines delivered via lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) or lipopolyplexes (LPPs) have a promising therapeutic potential as both prophylactic and therapeutic agents, supporting their advancement to clinical trials.

Although prophylactic virus-like particle (VLP) vaccines have been successfully implemented, they lack therapeutic efficacy against established infections and lesions in the host. The messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccine platform has emerged as a promising alternative, offering rapid manufacturing and the ability to induce potent cellular immune responses required for effective therapeutic outcomes. Objective This systematic review aimed to synthesize and evaluate preclinical evidence regarding the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of mRNA-based HPV vaccines in animal models, focusing on their ability to prevent oncogenic infections and induce regression of established tumors. Methods The study is registered in Prospero (CRD420261362037, 14 July 2026). A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Europe PMC, and ScienceDirect databases was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies included in vivo preclinical experimental research evaluating mRNA vaccines targeting high-risk HPV types (HPV-16 and HPV-18) in animal models. Immunogenicity (CD8+ T-cell responses and IgG titers) and oncogenic outcome (tumor volume and survival rate) data were extracted. The risk of bias was assessed using the SYRCLE’s risk-of-bias tool. The meta-analysis utilized a random-effects model to calculate standardized mean differences (SMD) and evaluate heterogeneity via the I 2 statistic. Result and Conclusion Ten studies met the inclusion criteria and provided detailed data for the analysis. mRNA vaccines have demonstrated high immunogenicity, significantly expanding antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell populations and inducing robust IFN gamma secretion. The pooled results indicated a significant reduction in tumor volume (SMD -2.305; 95% CI: −2.64 to −1.97) and near-complete viral load reduction in the challenge models. High-risk HPV mRNA vaccines delivered via lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) or lipopolyplexes (LPPs) have a promising therapeutic potential as both prophylactic and therapeutic agents, supporting their advancement to clinical trials.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPV), focusing on high-risk types (e.g., HPV-16, HPV-18) and their association with oncogenic outcomes such as cervical, anogenital, and oropharyngeal malignancies, as well as HPV infection and genital warts in the host. The central question evaluates the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of mRNA-based HPV vaccines in preclinical animal models, specifically their ability to prevent oncogenic infections and induce regression of established tumors.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review and meta-analysis is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261362037, 14 July 2026) and follows PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Europe PMC, and ScienceDirect. Eligible studies included in vivo preclinical experimental research evaluating mRNA vaccines targeting high-risk HPV types (HPV-16 and HPV-18) in animal models. Immunogenicity (CD8+ T-cell responses and IgG titers) and oncogenic outcome (tumor volume and survival rate) data were extracted. The risk of bias was assessed using SYRCLE’s tool, and a random-effects meta-analysis calculated standardized mean differences (SMD) with heterogeneity evaluated via the I2 statistic.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled results demonstrate that mRNA vaccines induce high immunogenicity, significantly expanding antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell populations and inducing robust IFN gamma secretion. There is a significant reduction in tumor volume (SMD -2.305; 95% CI: −2.64 to −1.97) and near-complete viral load reduction in challenge models. High-risk HPV mRNA vaccines delivered via lipid nanoparticles or lipopolyplexes show promising therapeutic potential as both prophylactic and therapeutic agents.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report long-term safety data, durability of immune responses, or comparative efficacy against established prophylactic virus-like particle (VLP) vaccines in humans. Additionally, the evidence base is limited to preclinical animal models, leaving uncertainties about translational potential to human clinical settings.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings support the advancement of mRNA-based HPV vaccines to clinical trials, particularly for therapeutic applications against established infections and lesions. title_zh: mRNA疫苗疫苗在诱导免疫应答和预防致癌结局中的有效性:一项系统综述与荟萃分析
source_body_en: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection represents a substantial global health burden, being the primary etiological agent of cervical cancer, anogenital and oropharyngeal malignancies. Although prophylactic virus-like particle (VLP) vaccines have been successfully implemented, they lack therapeutic efficacy against established infections and lesions in the host. The messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccine platform has emerged as a promising alternative, offering rapid manufacturing and the ability to induce potent cellular immune responses required for effective therapeutic outcomes. Objective This systematic review aimed to synthesize and evaluate preclinical evidence regarding the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of mRNA-based HPV vaccines in animal models, focusing on their ability to prevent oncogenic infections and induce regression of established tumors. Methods The study is registered in Prospero (CRD420261362037, 14 July 2026). A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Europe PMC, and ScienceDirect databases was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies included in vivo preclinical experimental research evaluating mRNA vaccines targeting high-risk HPV types (HPV-16 and HPV-18) in animal models. Immunogenicity (CD8+ T-cell responses and IgG titers) and oncogenic outcome (tumor volume and survival rate) data were extracted. The risk of bias was assessed using the SYRCLE’s risk-of-bias tool. The meta-analysis utilized a random-effects model to calculate standardized mean differences (SMD) and evaluate heterogeneity via the I 2 statistic. Result and Conclusion Ten studies met the inclusion criteria and provided detailed data for the analysis. mRNA vaccines have demonstrated high immunogenicity, significantly expanding antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell populations and inducing robust IFN gamma secretion. The pooled results indicated a significant reduction in tumor volume (SMD -2.305; 95% CI: −2.64 to −1.97) and near-complete viral load reduction in the challenge models. High-risk HPV mRNA vaccines delivered via lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) or lipopolyplexes (LPPs) have a promising therapeutic potential as both prophylactic and therapeutic agents, supporting their advancement to clinical trials.

title: Penile Intraepithelial Neoplasia and Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Contemporary Review of Clinicopathologic Features, Classification, and Prognostication.
abstract: ABSTRACT Penile intraepithelial neoplasia is an uncommon precancerous genital lesion that may progress to invasive penile squamous cell carcinoma in the absence of proper therapeutic management. The recent trend of increasing incidence because of a heightened burden of genital human papillomavirus (HPV) infection emphasizes a need for effective diagnostic and management strategies. This article provides a clinicopathologic overview focusing on updates in tumor classification and prognostication not previously summarized. We examine changes in classification and nomenclature based on the 2022 World Health Organization guidelines and explore differences in pathogenesis and prognosis between HPV-associated and HPV-independent tumors. This article emphasizes the need for more robust molecular genetic studies to further elucidate prognostic biomarkers and explores the increasingly distinct role of immunohistochemistry in stratifying subtypes. Also, we present an illustrative case to highlight the significance of accurate diagnosis and prompt management.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPV) and their association with penile intraepithelial neoplasia (PeIN) and penile squamous cell carcinoma (PSCC), focusing on the central question of how HPV-driven pathogenesis and classification updates inform diagnostic and prognostic strategies for these HPV-associated genital lesions.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a contemporary clinicopathologic overview summarizing updates in tumor classification and prognostication based on the 2022 World Health Organization guidelines, with a focus on distinguishing HPV-associated from HPV-independent penile tumors.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that penile intraepithelial neoplasia is a precancerous lesion with potential progression to invasive penile squamous cell carcinoma without proper management, and emphasizes the increasing incidence of HPV-associated penile lesions due to rising genital HPV infection burden.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies a need for more robust molecular genetic studies to elucidate prognostic biomarkers and to clarify the distinct roles of immunohistochemistry in stratifying HPV-associated versus HPV-independent penile tumor subtypes.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review underscores the importance of accurate diagnosis and prompt management of penile intraepithelial neoplasia to prevent progression to invasive carcinoma, and calls for improved diagnostic and management strategies in the context of rising HPV-associated disease incidence.

title_zh: 阴茎上皮内瘤变和鳞状细胞癌:临床病理特征、分类和预后的当代回顾。
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Penile intraepithelial neoplasia is an uncommon precancerous genital lesion that may progress to invasive penile squamous cell carcinoma in the absence of proper therapeutic management. The recent trend of increasing incidence because of a heightened burden of genital human papillomavirus (HPV) infection emphasizes a need for effective diagnostic and management strategies. This article provides a clinicopathologic overview focusing on updates in tumor classification and prognostication not previously summarized. We examine changes in classification and nomenclature based on the 2022 World Health Organization guidelines and explore differences in pathogenesis and prognosis between HPV-associated and HPV-independent tumors. This article emphasizes the need for more robust molecular genetic studies to further elucidate prognostic biomarkers and explores the increasingly distinct role of immunohistochemistry in stratifying subtypes. Also, we present an illustrative case to highlight the significance of accurate diagnosis and prompt management.

title: Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine Special Statement: Reducing the risk of transmitting infection during ultrasound examination—Updated 2026
abstract: Abstract Ultrasound examinations have the potential to transmit infections between individuals. The risk can be reduced by following certain well‐described procedures to clean and disinfect ultrasound transducers between examinations. However, surveys have shown widespread lapses in the cleaning and disinfection of transducers and other equipment. In 2020, the Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine (SMFM) published a Patient Safety Guideline focused on reducing the risk of transmitting infection in transvaginal examinations, with emphasis on selection of high‐level disinfectants with proven efficacy against human papillomavirus (HPV), choice of transducer covers with documented low leakage rates, and cautions regarding multiuse containers of coupling gel. In this article, SMFM presents updated guidelines with an expanded scope that includes transabdominal examinations and ultrasound‐guided percutaneous and intraoperative procedures. Other updates include a list of newer high‐level disinfection systems and citation of recent literature on virucidal efficacy of ortho‐phthalaldehyde against HPV. The guidelines are based on the Spaulding classification of infection risk and are aligned with recommendations from the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and the US Food and Drug Administration. This Special Statement replaces Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine Special Statement: Reducing the risk of transmitting infection by transvaginal ultrasound examination, 2020 .
authors: SMFM Patient Safety and Quality Committee

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPV), specifically high-risk HPV types such as HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, HPV33, HPV45, HPV52, and HPV58, and their association with diseases like cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, HPV-associated cervical cancer, HPV-associated anal cancer, HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer, genital warts, and anogenital warts. The central question is how to reduce the risk of transmitting HPV during ultrasound examinations, particularly transvaginal, transabdominal, and ultrasound-guided procedures.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is an updated guideline from the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine (SMFM) that incorporates recent literature and new disinfection systems. It references the Spaulding classification of infection risk and aligns with recommendations from the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and the US Food and Drug Administration. The review includes surveys highlighting lapses in cleaning and disinfection practices.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the risk of transmitting HPV during ultrasound examinations can be reduced by following procedures to clean and disinfect ultrasound transducers between uses. It emphasizes the use of high-level disinfectants with proven efficacy against HPV, particularly ortho-phthalaldehyde, and the importance of transducer covers with low leakage rates. The guidelines also caution against the use of multiuse containers of coupling gel.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that surveys have shown widespread lapses in the cleaning and disinfection of transducers and other equipment, indicating a gap in adherence to recommended practices. There is no explicit mention of controversies, but the lack of consistent implementation suggests unresolved issues in practice.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends updating disinfection protocols, using newer high-level disinfection systems, and ensuring proper training for healthcare providers to prevent HPV transmission during ultrasound procedures. It also highlights the need for ongoing surveillance and adherence to guidelines to reduce infection risks.

analysis.summary_en: This review updates guidelines for reducing the risk of transmitting human papillomaviruses (HPV) during ultrasound examinations, including transvaginal, transabdominal, and ultrasound-guided procedures. It emphasizes the importance of cleaning and disinfecting transducers with high-level disinfectants proven effective against HPV, such as ortho-phthalaldehyde, and the use of transducer covers with low leakage rates. The review highlights widespread lapses in adherence to these practices and aligns with recommendations from multiple authoritative bodies. The guidelines aim to improve infection control through updated protocols and provider training.

title_zh: 母胎医学学会特别声明:降低超声检查期间感染传播风险——2026年更新
source_body_en: Abstract Ultrasound examinations have the potential to transmit infections between individuals. The risk can be reduced by following certain well‐described procedures to clean and disinfect ultrasound transducers between examinations. However, surveys have shown widespread lapses in the cleaning and disinfection of transducers and other equipment. In 2020, the Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine (SMFM) published a Patient Safety Guideline focused on reducing the risk of transmitting infection in transvaginal examinations, with emphasis on selection of high‐level disinfectants with proven efficacy against human papillomavirus (HPV), choice of transducer covers with documented low leakage rates, and cautions regarding multiuse containers of coupling gel. In this article, SMFM presents updated guidelines with an expanded scope that includes transabdominal examinations and ultrasound‐guided percutaneous and intraoperative procedures. Other updates include a list of newer high‐level disinfection systems and citation of recent literature on virucidal efficacy of ortho‐phthalaldehyde against HPV. The guidelines are based on the Spaulding classification of infection risk and are aligned with recommendations from the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and the US Food and Drug Administration. This Special Statement replaces Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine Special Statement: Reducing the risk of transmitting infection by transvaginal ultrasound examination, 2020 .

title: Application of Cobas 6800 HPV testing and qPCR utilizing three genomically-optimized primer sets for detecting HPV DNA in the blood of HPV Positive dysplasia and cancer patients
abstract: Use of quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) to measure viral DNA in plasma has promise for the detection and/or monitoring of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV)-associated cancers. We examined Roche’s cobas 6800 HPV test for detection of hrHPV in plasma or peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) of patients with HPV-associated dysplasia or cancer. In our pilot study, this assay detected hrHPV DNA in 1 mL pre-treatment plasma of patients with advanced (stage II-IV) cervical cancer, but not stage I or dysplasia cases, or in PBMC. Plasma of oropharyngeal cancer patients also tested positive in most cases. Seeking to enhance sensitivity, we re-tested these pilot samples with qPCR employing three published primer sets (E7, BR E1-5, HR E5L2-4) selected for improved detection of HPV16 in cancer. This triplex assay detected quantifiable levels of HPV16 in pre-treatment plasma of advanced (stage II-IV) cervical cancer cases, and lower levels in some stage I and dysplasia cases. In serial sampling of HPV16 + cervical cancer patients post-treatment with no evidence of disease over ~2 years, no reproducible signal was detected by cobas HPV testing, whereas the triplex qPCR sporadically detected HPV DNA in plasma and PBMC samples of a subset of these patients.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the utility of qPCR for detecting HPV DNA in plasma and to explore its potential for monitoring hrHPV-associated cancers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A pilot study was conducted using pre-treatment plasma samples from patients with advanced cervical cancer, stage I cervical cancer, and HPV-associated dysplasia, as well as oropharyngeal cancer patients.
analysis.methods: The study employed Roche’s cobas 6800 HPV test and triplex qPCR with three genomically-optimized primer sets (E7, BR E1-5, HR E5L2-4) to detect HPV16 and other hrHPV types in plasma samples.
analysis.main_results: The cobas HPV test detected hrHPV DNA in advanced cervical cancer plasma but not in stage I or dysplasia cases or PBMC. The triplex qPCR detected quantifiable HPV16 levels in advanced cervical cancer plasma and lower levels in some stage I and dysplasia cases. Post-treatment serial sampling showed no reproducible signal with cobas testing, but sporadic HPV DNA detection was observed in a subset of patients using triplex qPCR.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The triplex qPCR demonstrated improved sensitivity for detecting HPV16 in plasma compared to the cobas test, suggesting its potential for more accurate monitoring of HPV-associated cancers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of more sensitive diagnostic tools for HPV-associated cancers, particularly in plasma-based detection, which could enhance surveillance and monitoring strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to a pilot sample size and focused on HPV16, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to the exploratory nature of the study and the lack of long-term follow-up data.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the use of qPCR with three genomically-optimized primer sets for detecting HPV DNA in plasma from patients with HPV-associated dysplasia and cancer. The cobas 6800 HPV test detected hrHPV in advanced cervical cancer plasma but not in stage I or dysplasia cases or PBMC. The triplex qPCR showed improved sensitivity for HPV16 detection in plasma and some stage I and dysplasia cases. Post-treatment serial sampling revealed no reproducible signal with cobas testing, but sporadic HPV DNA detection was observed in a subset of patients using triplex qPCR. The triplex qPCR demonstrated potential for more accurate monitoring of HPV-associated cancers, which could inform improved diagnostic strategies. However, the study's limited sample size and focus on HPV16 may restrict its generalizability, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Immunological consequences of mesenchymal stem cell therapy in HPV-driven cervical cancer: a systematic review and stratification framework.
abstract: Over 660,000 women develop cervical cancer annually, caused by persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV). Published studies of mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) as immunomodulatory agents are contradictory, with some reporting tumor suppression and others tumor promotion. The mechanism of these paradoxes has not been systematically investigated. This review aims to assess MSC-mediated immune evasion in HPV-related cervical cancer, quantify HPV stratification failure in the literature, and formulate a predictive stratification model linking MSC behavior to HPV oncogenic activity. A systematic review was performed following PRISMA 2020 guidelines across 8 databases. Studies were included if they reported an MSC intervention for cervical cancer with one or more immune-related outcomes. HPV stratification gap analysis was performed alongside data extraction and risk-of-bias evaluation. 14 studies were included: 13 completed preclinical and 1 ongoing clinical trial. MSC effects included immune evasion through adenosine, IL-10, and M2 macrophage polarization, and tumor suppression through STAT3, Wnt/β-Catenin, and epigenetic pathways. Of 13 completed studies, none measured HPV oncogenic activity as an experimental variable. Only two included an HPV-negative cohort. Differential effects of MSC exosomes on HPV16 and HPV18 cell lines were recorded but not linked to HPV genotype. HPV oncogenic activity is an unmeasured and plausible modifier of MSC activity in cervical cancer. Stratification by HPV oncogenic status should be a methodological requirement for interpretable and translatable evidence, because E6/E7 signalling is linked to PDL-1, TGF-β, STAT-3 and NF-κB, all linked to MSC immunomodulatory pathways. A predictive stratification system and minimum reporting standards are suggested.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the immunological effects of mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) in HPV-driven cervical cancer. It highlights the contradictory findings in the literature regarding MSCs' role in tumor suppression or promotion. The review identifies a critical gap in understanding the mechanisms behind these paradoxes and emphasizes the need for HPV stratification in future studies. It suggests that HPV oncogenic activity, particularly through E6/E7 signaling, influences MSC behavior and that stratification by HPV status is essential for generating interpretable and translatable evidence. The review also proposes a predictive stratification model and minimum reporting standards to improve the quality and relevance of future research.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 每年有超过 660,000 名女性患有 宫颈癌,这是由高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 持续感染引起的。本综述旨在评估 HPV 相关 宫颈癌 中 MSC 介导的免疫逃避,量化文献中的 HPV 分层失败,并制定将 MSC 行为与 HPV 致癌活性联系起来的预测分层模型。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 根据 PRISMA 2020 指南对 8 个数据库进行了系统评价。已发表的间充质干细胞/基质细胞(MSC)作为免疫调节剂的研究是相互矛盾的,一些报告抑制肿瘤,另一些报告促进肿瘤。如果研究报告 MSC 干预 宫颈癌 并产生一种或多种免疫相关结果,则研究被纳入。HPV 分层差距分析与数据提取和偏倚风险评估一起进行。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: MSC 的作用包括通过腺苷、IL-10 和 M2 巨噬细胞极化进行免疫逃避,以及通过 STAT3、Wnt/β-Catenin 和表观遗传途径抑制肿瘤。HPV 致癌活性是 宫颈癌 中 MSC 活性的未测量且合理的修饰因子。建议采用预测分层系统和最低报告标准。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 这些悖论的机制尚未得到系统研究。在 13 项已完成的研究中,没有一项研究将 HPV 致癌活性作为实验变量进行测量。记录了 MSC 外泌体对 HPV16 和 HPV18 细胞系的不同影响,但与 HPV 基因型无关。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 按 HPV 致癌状态进行分层应该是可解释和可翻译证据的方法学要求,因为 E6/E7 信号传导与 PDL-1、TGF-β、STAT-3 和 NF-κB 相关,所有这些都与 MSC 免疫调节途径相关。

title: Long-term trends and post-pandemic deviations in cervical cancer burden in South India, 1990-2023: a Global Burden of Disease 2023 study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Cervical cancer remains a major public health challenge in India despite advances in prevention through human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination and screening. Although national estimates indicate gradual declines, marked regional disparities persist, and coronavirus disease 2019-related disruptions may have affected recent disease trajectories. This study assessed long-term trends, post-pandemic deviations, and progress toward World Health Organization (WHO) elimination targets in South India. METHODS: This population-based observational analysis used Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 estimates for women aged 30-69 years in South India from 1990 to 2023. Pre-pandemic trends and counterfactual projections were evaluated, and age-standardized incidence rates (ASRs) were descriptively compared with the WHO elimination threshold of ≤4 cases per 100,000 woman-years. RESULTS: Age-standardized cervical cancer incidence and mortality declined until the early 2010s but remained above national and global rates. Thereafter, declines stagnated and reversed. In 2023, incidence ranged from 26.1 per 100,000 women in Kerala to 65.8 in Telangana; all states exceeded the WHO threshold based on these ASRs. Observed rates exceeded counterfactual projections, but uncertainty envelopes included zero for every location and outcome. Thus, the findings are consistent with possible post-pandemic disruption to cervical cancer services rather than statistically demonstrated excess burden, and this ecological comparison cannot establish causality. Disability-adjusted life-year rates were highest among women aged 50-69 years. CONCLUSION: South India appears to have experienced a recent loss of momentum in cervical cancer control. Strengthening HPV vaccination coverage, expanding screening, and improving the resilience of cancer prevention services are essential for accelerating progress toward elimination targets.
journal: Osong Public Health and Research Perspectives
